note: Farming systems a farmer can choose. crops_min/crops_max bound the selection; the layout engine renders each system differently. usable_area_fraction is the share of gross land actually planted after field bunds/borders, walking & inspection paths and irrigation lines — plant counts, inputs and economics scale to it.

systems.name: Single crop
systems.area_note: ~5% reserved for field bunds, borders and turning space.
systems.description: One crop across the whole field — paddy, wheat, cotton and other traditional field crops. Simplest to manage and mechanise.
systems.best_for: Staple grains, assured-irrigation fields, mechanised farms

systems.name: Intercropping
systems.area_note: ~8% reserved for bunds, access rows and irrigation channels.
systems.description: Two or three crops in alternating row bands (e.g. 2 rows maize : 1 row soybean). Spreads risk and improves per-acre income; legume partners add nitrogen.
systems.best_for: Rain-fed fields, risk reduction, soil health

systems.name: Multi-layer farming
systems.area_note: ~20% reserved for walking/inspection paths, drip lines and working space between beds.
systems.description: Up to five vertical layers — canopy fruit trees, climbers, bushy vegetables, leafy ground cover and root crops sharing the same land. Highest income per acre; more labour and know-how.
systems.best_for: Small holdings, horticulture belts, maximum revenue per acre
